subject.title: Feature request: Persistent task-status surface for long-running channel turns

question: Should OpenClaw add a persistent per-channel-turn status surface, and should its canonical owner be runtime/session activity, the task ledger, or channel transport?
rationale: The remaining work is not a missing line of code; the owner choice determines persistence, restart semantics, Discord rollout, config defaults, and how existing progress drafts/status reactions/task surfaces avoid becoming competing sources of truth.

options.title: Add runtime-owned status contract
options.body: Create an additive canonical status model in core/runtime and let Discord project it first as a best-effort editable message.

options.title: Use current progress drafts only
options.body: Treat progress drafts, status reactions, and task/status commands as sufficient and narrow this issue to docs or specific bug reports.

options.title: Start from durable runtime work
options.body: Wait for durable runtime direction to land, then build channel status projections on top of that canonical runtime state.

recommendation.title: Add runtime-owned status contract
recommendation.body: Create an additive canonical status model in core/runtime and let Discord project it first as a best-effort editable message.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available routing candidate for the task-state ownership side and broader product decision, while Discord/progress implementation history is shared with recent contributors.
